headline: Highest risk is medium: Claude Code can write shared files/git while python-cheatsheet is read-only, creating default-path prompt-injection and cascading-error exposure; no direct data-leak or compliance breach is evident.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Claude Code can read/write the filesystem, modify git state, and use MCP; python-cheatsheet is documentation-only and cannot ingest outputs itself. The interaction pathway is via shared files/git, so if Claude Code later parses content from the repo or user directories as instructions, prompt injection is plausible in default coding workflows. The blast radius is limited to the workspace, not a broader channel.
conditions: IF Claude Code reads repo files or git-tracked content as instructions without provenance checks, injection is possible.
IF the pair is connected only by manual copy-paste, severity drops to low.
mitigations: Add a provenance banner to any B-generated text before Claude Code consumes it.
Keep B outputs in a separate read-only notes file.
Require Claude Code to treat markdown/code fences as data unless explicitly promoted.
Disable MCP sources that can write into the shared workspace.
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization or instruction/data separation in the orchestrator.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Claude Code touches source code, git history, shell environment, and secrets, but python-cheatsheet has no filesystem, network, or API surfaces and touches no data classes. There is no plausible path for B to exfiltrate A's data by itself, and A's broad egress does not create leakage from B because B does not receive sensitive inputs. The pair therefore has only a small leakage risk if users manually copy secrets into B.
conditions: IF a user manually pastes secrets from Claude Code into python-cheatsheet outputs, leakage becomes possible.
IF B is replaced with a networked agent, reassess upward.
mitigations: Do not paste secrets into B.
Keep B outputs free of repo paths and credentials.
Use redacted examples when moving text from A to B.
Review any copied snippets before sharing externally.
requires-engineering: route sensitive work to a segregated workspace.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Claude Code has unrestricted filesystem write and git modification in the invoking user session, while python-cheatsheet is non-runnable and read-only. There is no direct write-write conflict, but if B's content is copied into the same repo, A can overwrite or commit it without locking. Because A's concurrency model shares state via filesystem and git only, the overlap is real in default coding setups, though B itself cannot contend actively.
conditions: IF B content is stored in the same git working tree that Claude Code edits, write conflicts are possible.
IF the orchestrator provides file locks, severity drops to low.
mitigations: Keep B artifacts outside the repo.
Commit A changes before importing B text.
Use per-agent subdirectories.
Avoid concurrent edits to the same files.
requires-engineering: add locking around shared git operations.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Claude Code can generate code or facts that a content-writing agent could render, but python-cheatsheet is documentation-only and does not execute actions. The main risk is that B may present A's output as authoritative without verification if the workflow copies text from A into B. That creates a default-path misinformation cascade, but not an action-taking one, so medium fits better than high.
conditions: IF B republishes A's output without checking sources, cascading error is possible.
IF B is used only as a static reference, severity is low.
mitigations: Require source links for any factual claim copied from A.
Have B label A-derived text as unverified.
Cross-check critical statements against primary docs.
Keep generated summaries separate from final deliverables.
requires-engineering: add automated citation validation.

E_compliance.rationale: Claude Code handles git credentials and may process source code and shell environment data, while python-cheatsheet is documentation-only and touches no regulated data classes. No residency, retention, or certification mismatch is evidenced in the profiles, and B has no data handling surface that would create a compliance breach. The only cited agent needing mention is A because B is effectively inert for compliance purposes.
conditions: IF regulated data is manually copied into B, reassess compliance impact.
IF B gains storage or network features, reassess upward.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of B.
Use sanitized examples only.
Document that B is reference-only.
Separate credentials from working notes.
requires-engineering: add policy enforcement for regulated datasets.
